cost: fill may expand repeatedly: cost is sum of intermediate string lengths plus replacement bytes. run stores complete stdout/stderr, memory O(output), child time and DB effects unbounded.
description: run selects DUCKDB or HOME/bin/duckdb, spawns -bail -batch plus optional mode and db, writes SQL then waits; nonzero status or stderr Error: returns error, otherwise stdout is decoded lossily. fill folds ordered global replacements after doubling apostrophes.
forward: run selects DUCKDB or HOME/bin/duckdb, spawns -bail -batch plus optional mode and db, writes SQL then waits; nonzero status or stderr Error: returns error, otherwise stdout is decoded lossily. fill folds ordered global replacements after doubling apostrophes.
inverse: If spawn fails, no SQL is written to a child by this call. If status is failure or stderr contains exact Error:, wrapper cannot return Ok(stdout). No claim that every DB failure uses that marker.

Given final SQL, reconstruct all original templates and ordered variable arrays whose repeated escaped substitutions yield it. Literal text and inserted values are indistinguishable; run output cannot uniquely reconstruct SQL, DB state or child diagnostics.
limitations: No network/DNS/download, real catalog/corpus/model/teacher or database execution. Effect paths are source-derived; finite helper tests are not universal verification. No executable percentage surrogate or speed claim; future caps require metric/domain/reference and remain 1/2/5/10%.
state: Successful OS status is necessary but insufficient for wrapper success. Replacement order is observable; mode is a single argv element. No SQL parser or prepared statement semantics is supplied.
